segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 25, 2026.
We've got 16 updates, including news on major acquisitions, humanoid robot programs, and advancements in physical AI.
Tune in for the latest!
From The Robot Report, SoftBank acquires Marc Raibert’s Robotics and AI Institute.
This report details the acquisition of the Robotics and AI Institute by SoftBank, which adds another significant robotics entity to the conglomerate's portfolio.
The acquisition involves SoftBank taking over the Robotics and AI Institute from Hyundai Motor Group.
The institute was founded by Marc Raibert and focuses on fundamental robotics challenges including mobility, manipulation, and intelligence.
This transaction creates potential synergies between the institute's ongoing research and other entities within SoftBank's investment portfolio.
The Robotics and AI Institute is currently seeking to expand its team by filling various open positions across different robotics technologies.
This development signals an integration of advanced robotics research into a major technology investment group.
The industry should monitor future collaborations arising from this integration.
From Humanoid.guide, Türkiye launches humanoid robot program with 50% grants.
This report details the initiation of a national program offering substantial financial support to develop domestic industrial humanoid robots.

The program is specifically focused on bipedal machines intended for manufacturing assembly, logistics, and precision machining, with funding provided at a fifty percent grant rate over a period extending up to forty-eight months.
The initiative mandates that developed robots must be at least one point six meters in height and possess multi-tasking capabilities, alongside defined specifications for lifting and mobility.
A primary goal of this effort is the domestic development of essential components such as actuators, sensors, and software architecture.
Applications submitted for evaluation will be assessed based on demonstrated innovation, economic value, and social impact.
This move signals a concentrated effort to build indigenous capabilities within the robotics and artificial intelligence sectors.
Further developments in domestic hardware and software solutions are anticipated in the coming months.
From Robotics & Automation News, Siemens advances physical AI and autonomous production technologies.
This report details Siemens' integration of artificial intelligence to enable autonomous production through AI-powered planning, engineering, and physical AI applications on factory floors.
The company demonstrated goal-based automation in their Electronics Factory with an AI-powered robotic system that autonomously unpacks goods using real-time camera input.
Furthermore, the Autonomous Production Planner utilizes collaborating AI agents and physics-based digital twins to optimize schedules, with the potential to reduce manual planning by seventy percent.

Siemens is also enhancing its AI by incorporating agents that adapt automation code and integrating artificial intelligence directly into machine control systems, underscoring the need for cybersecurity in industrial AI compliance with regulations such as the European Union's Cyber Resilience Act.
This development signals a progression toward fully autonomous industrial environments.
From Humanoid.guide, Roscosmos launches Teledroid humanoid for ISS exterior work.

This report details the launch of the Teledroid humanoid robot toward the International Space Station on November 24, 2026, designed to prepare exterior work sites by opening casings and installing equipment ahead of spacewalks.
The robot was deployed aboard the Progress MS-36.
Teledroid integrates operator motion copying with autonomous task execution, allowing control from within the station or ground control.
Control hardware, including a necessary workstation, was delivered before the launch.
Future operations will involve crew training and physical installation outside the Nauka module.
This development signals advancements in remote manipulation and autonomous robotics for complex extravehicular activities.
From The Robot Report, Robotics Summit 2027 opens call for speakers.
This announcement details the invitation for session abstracts for the upcoming Robotics Summit and Expo.
The summit, scheduled for June 2 to 3 in Boston, is set to attract over five thousand attendees and focus on the technical development of commercial robots.
Session topics are organized into tracks encompassing technologies, design, artificial intelligence, coding, logistics, and healthcare robotics.
The deadline for submitting speaker proposals is December 30, 2026, and accepted speakers will receive complimentary full conference registration.
This initiative aims to gather specialized knowledge from the industry.
The upcoming summit signals an increased focus on practical, applied robotics research and commercial deployment within the artificial intelligence and technology sectors.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Reliability emerges as the next big challenge for robotics".
This report details the growing necessity for ensuring the reliable, consistent, and safe operation of robots over extended periods across various industrial applications.
Developers are increasingly integrating Design for Reliability methodologies and employing engineering software to proactively assess system weaknesses during the development phase.
Operational data gathered from sensors is being utilized to refine both system designs and subsequent maintenance strategies.
This focus on reliability is establishing itself as a critical competitive differentiator determining the success and scalability of future robotics ventures.
The industry must prioritize robust reliability engineering to support the advancement of artificial intelligence and automation technologies.
From Robotics & Automation News, researcher develops quantum-inspired approach to safer autonomous drone navigation.

This story details the development of a quantum-inspired decision-support framework intended to enhance the safety and reliability of autonomous drone navigation by integrating operational risks into route planning.

The research involved creating a system that evaluates potential routes based on a combination of energy consumption, prevailing weather conditions, and established safety requirements, moving beyond simple shortest-route calculations.

Simulations demonstrated that this new framework achieved a reduction in route risk by twenty point five percent and a decrease in safety rule violations by fifty-two point eight percent when compared to existing navigation methods.
While an increase in energy consumption was observed, the findings support the implementation of knowledge-based systems for more dependable autonomous flight.
This work indicates a trajectory toward more robust and safer autonomous aerial systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Bentic prepares for US expansion as physical AI robot installations approach 100.
This report details the advancement of physical artificial intelligence in industrial automation, noting that nearly one hundred robots are currently deployed handling deformable materials.
The company's technology allows robots to manage tasks involving textiles, cables, carbon fiber, and food, materials that have historically resisted conventional automation methods.
Bentic achieves this by training its artificial intelligence using real-world industrial data gathered directly from production environments, moving beyond reliance on simulation.
The system integrates predictive intelligence with action models to facilitate the manipulation of these complex materials.
The company is currently planning for expansion into the United States, targeting the deployment of its systems there by the end of 2026.
This development indicates a growing commercial application for physical AI in challenging industrial settings.
From Humanoids Daily, Adcock Answers Musk's Apple Challenge With a Figure 03 Clip.
This report details a demonstration of autonomous task completion by a humanoid robot following a table relocation.
Brett Adcock presented a Figure 03 clip illustrating the robot's ability to successfully pick up an apple from a table that had been moved.

The demonstration highlighted that the Figure AI Helix model achieved zero-shot, fully autonomous performance in this scenario, directly addressing claims regarding the limitations of current humanoid robot programming.
This achievement suggests a capability for robots to perform arbitrary tasks with unfamiliar objects, aligning with the broader goals of the AI research sector.
Further development from Figure AI aims for robots to handle multi-hour chores in any home within six months.
This development signals progress toward more general artificial intelligence in physical environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Where eagles dare: XPeng’s physical AI ambitions prepare for take-off".
This report details XPeng's pursuit of physical artificial intelligence through the development of proprietary computing hardware for on-device AI execution across physical systems.

XPeng is developing components such as the Turing AI processor to facilitate the running of large artificial intelligence models directly on vehicles, robots, and flying vehicles, conceptualizing intelligent vehicles as robots on wheels that integrate AI into physical operations like steering and braking.

Furthermore, the company is developing a humanoid robot named Iron, leveraging its AI and computing strengths to demonstrate a focus on physical AI applications, a development supported by significant investment in the robotics sector.
This expansion indicates a strategy to apply advanced AI technology across tangible, real-world forms.
The trajectory suggests a growing integration of sophisticated AI into physical automation systems moving forward.
From Robotics & Automation News, Neuryn Robotics develops AI-powered robots to automate fashion returns, a development focused on streamlining the processing of returned apparel.
Neuryn Robotics, a startup based in Madrid, is currently developing robotic systems designed to automate the entire process of fashion e-commerce returns.
These robotic systems are engineered to handle tasks ranging from the unpacking of garments to the detailed inspection of their condition and subsequent determination of the appropriate next action.

The artificial intelligence within these systems assesses clothing items to categorize them for resale, repair, or recycling, effectively managing the complexity introduced by varied garment shapes and conditions.
This technology is intended to assist retailers in managing surplus inventory in compliance with environmental regulations.
Other robotics entities are also implementing comparable artificial intelligence solutions for managing fashion retailer returns.
This advancement indicates a growing application of sophisticated AI in the logistics and sustainability sectors.
From Robotics & Automation News, TÜV SÜD awards human-machine performance certification to Ascentiz exoskeletons.
This report details the independent assessment of Ascentiz's Pro and Ultra modular hip exoskeletons, which achieved certification based on performance across various indicators.
Independent testing across multiple performance metrics, including workload reduction, fatigue relief, range, and noise levels, involved seven everyday activities to assess the devices.
The testing revealed significant exertion decrease, including an over forty-four percent reduction in muscle group exertion during uphill walking.

Furthermore, the exoskeletons demonstrated a travel range exceeding six kilometers under demanding conditions and registered a peak hip extension torque of approximately twenty-two point five Newton meters per side.
This certification acknowledges Ascentiz's focus on user experience within the consumer exoskeleton sector.
This achievement establishes a benchmark for performance validation in assistive technology development.

From Robotics & Automation News, Path2 develops an online robot cell builder to make automation more accessible, demonstrating a method for reducing the cost and complexity of industrial robotics integration.
The platform is a browser-based system enabling smaller manufacturers to design and program robot workcells without large integration budgets.
Users utilize the platform to virtually position robots, conveyors, and safety guards, and teach robot movements directly on screen to automatically generate programs.
A demonstration showcased a layout for a running palletizing cycle achieved in nineteen minutes without manual code writing.

The platform currently supports twenty Kuka robot models and will expand to other major manufacturers, offering engineering packages and safety guidance through a structure of design packages and subscriptions.
This development indicates a pathway for democratizing advanced automation tools for smaller industrial operations.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Ramp Autonomy: a ROS 2 / Gazebo stack for ramp ascent and descent on a loaded AMR".
This story details a ROS 2 and Gazebo stack developed for ramp ascent and descent on a loaded Autonomous Mobile Robot.
The system successfully addresses navigation challenges encountered on inclines by managing IMU bias, center of gravity shifts, and wheel slip.
The framework utilizes a five-state Finite State Machine, integrates a LiDAR slope classifier, and incorporates safety layers to handle the dynamic changes during traversal.
Specific findings included observations regarding MPPI profile asymmetry and the effect of speed capping on wheel slip during descent.
This research contributes to the development of more robust navigation systems for mobile robotics in complex environments.
From CMU Robotics Institute, Knitting a New Future for Robot Fashion.
This report details a collaboration between students from Carnegie Mellon University and Kent State University that resulted in a win at the Humanoid Robot Fashion Challenge.

The winning team utilized computational textile design to develop an outfit for a humanoid robot, exploring functional and movable garments by integrating skills from textile design, coding, and fashion.
This process highlighted the significance of how robots will be perceived based on their visual appearance and interaction with human observers.
The winning designs are scheduled to be featured at a Robot Fashion event during New York Fashion Week.
This achievement signals a growing focus on the aesthetic and interactive design aspects of artificial intelligence and robotics.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Zipline and Chipotle complete first drone food delivery in PGA Tour history".
This report details the successful execution of the first drone food delivery in PGA Tour history between Zipline and Chipotle.
The operation involved drones dropping meals directly onto a golf course for professional golfers Joel Dahmen and Mark Hubbard during a practice round in Austin, Texas.
Dahmen received a steak bowl, and Hubbard received a steak burrito with guacamole.

Chipotle collaborated with Zipline to extend delivery services to unconventional locations such as golf courses, demonstrating the feasibility of autonomous aerial delivery systems for novel delivery scenarios.
This event illustrates the growing potential of autonomous aerial technology for expanding logistical capabilities across diverse environments.
And that's all the circuits for today, November 25th, 2026.
SoftBank is adding some serious smarts to the robotic world!
Thanks for plugging into the future with us.
See you tomorrow!
